runs.text:
In this four-class micro-Doppler radar target classification study, four machine learning models were evaluated using nested $5\times5$ measurement-grouped cross-validation on 75,801 segments from 130 measurements. All models significantly outperformed the majority baseline (macro $F_1$: 0.2183). 

The RBF-SVM achieved the highest overall performance, yielding a mean macro $F_1$-score of 0.8771 ($\pm$0.0248) and 93.79% accuracy. XGBoost followed closely with a macro $F_1$ of 0.8625 ($\pm$0.0369) and 93.00% accuracy, while demonstrating superior computational efficiency with a training time of only 161.4 seconds. Random Forest and MLP achieved comparable macro $F_1$-scores of 0.8353 and 0.8338, respectively. Although the MLP achieved the lowest Expected Calibration Error (ECE: 0.0209), it required the longest training time (6,711.2 seconds). 

Overall, RBF-SVM provides the highest classification accuracy, while XGBoost offers an exceptionally efficient alternative with highly competitive performance.

*   **MLP** (3108 parameters): mean macro F1 of 0.8338 (std: 0.0305), accuracy of 0.9137, ECE of 0.0209, Brier score of 0.1276, and wall seconds of 6711.2.
